answer: Honest accounts carry a pearl: a deposit that grows with the account's own activity, never a flat entry fee. Idle keys out in the tundra of the ledger cost nothing, so sybils love cheap doors; a sliding bond makes each extra clone raise its own stake. Then audit at random: weekly the glacier of accumulated bonds is sampled, one account must show a signed history on short notice, and failure slashes its pearl to honest neighbors. Fifty fakes mean fifty multiplied stakes and fifty times the lottery risk - self-cloning stops being free and becomes a bad bet.
